epic.title: Prose instruction is a liability: put what can be checked behind a check
epic.intent_and_why: A hand-authored check is the same liability one level up, and it does not go away by making the author more capable. Wave 6 makes the check a generated artifact instead of a typed string.

definition_of_done: A spec format exists that an author can write without knowing the engine's JSON shape.
A generator emits a spine from it and refuses any spec whose output scripts/validate_spine.py would reject.
Every generated gate carries a place to record beliefs, concerns and open questions, in substrate the engine already renders.
A large claim is carried up to whoever reviews it rather than sitting inside a gate nobody opens.
Role specs exist for at least the implementer and the reviewer.
A spine generated from one is proven to drive to a terminal state in a real dispatch.

good_enough.mandatory_quality: The oracle does not move; no shipped template is edited to make output validate; every change gets a cold reviewer independent of its implementer.
good_enough.sufficient_evidence: Commands and their output, re-run by the Commander rather than accepted from a crew's report; a measured negative reported with the same rigor as a win.
good_enough.appetite: One bounded wave, generous compute, prefer another review round over shipping something unproven.

hard_constraints: checklist_engine.py's on-disk format is not changed.
validate_spine.py's fault set and acceptance boundary are not moved.
Beliefs, concerns and open questions ride in constraints/directives, never a new field the engine ignores.
No shipped template is edited to make generator output validate.
Implementers and reviewers run on Sonnet.
No issues are filed this wave; triage candidates route to the Admiral.
fixed_decisions: spec-has-no-raw-command-field: the spec offers a closed vocabulary of typed check kinds and no free-text shell field.
notes-live-in-directives-not-constraints: constraints already means rules-this-gate-must-respect on 970 live tasks.
handback-names-verbs-not-arrays: no engine verb appends to a directives field on an active gate.
escalation-is-review-result-APPROVE on gated, and stated-not-injected on survey.
placeholder-template-vs-instance: the generator refuses an instance carrying a non-resolver placeholder.

current_wave.objective: Write the thing that writes spines, and prove one drives.
exit_criteria: scripts/generate_spine.py exists, is cold-reviewed, and refuses what the oracle would refuse, shown as a paired control.
specs/implementer.spine.toml and specs/reviewer.spine.toml generate spines the oracle accepts with zero undecidable.
A generated spine reaches a terminal state under run_crew.py --spine, judged on spine_terminal.
The settling question is answered without softening.

issues.title: The generator
issues.desired_outcome: A spine generated from a typed spec, refused before emission if the oracle would reject it.
issues.useful_now: Nothing in the corpus wrote a good spine; validate_spine.py could only refuse a bad one.
issues.appetite: One crew gate with cold review.
issues.acceptance_or_falsification_evidence: The control pairing: one spec whose translation completes on the pure path and which the guarded CLI refuses with nothing written, and the same spec corrected and written.
issues.implementation_latitude: Module internals, CLI shape, error messages.
hard_constraints_no_gos: validate_spine.py is imported and called, never re-implemented or modified.
local_unknowns: Whether a closed vocabulary can express the two role specs without a raw-command field.

issues.title: The role specs
issues.desired_outcome: Implementer and reviewer role specs written in the format and generating clean.
issues.useful_now: It is the only way to find out whether the format removed the defect or moved it.
issues.appetite: One crew gate with cold review; it took two rounds.
issues.acceptance_or_falsification_evidence: Both generated spines OK with zero undecidable; the shipped <exact test command> placeholder replaced by a selector and a number.
issues.implementation_latitude: Which gates the specs carry and where the large claim sits.
local_unknowns: Whether the format can express a survey as well as a gated plan.

issues.title: The dispatch proof
issues.desired_outcome: A generated spine drives to a terminal state in a real dispatch.
issues.useful_now: Protected intent #4; without it the generator is unproven in the only place that counts.
issues.appetite: One dispatch plus a cold review of the proof.
issues.acceptance_or_falsification_evidence: The driven spine's own final state: every item complete or skipped, lease released, judged by run_crew on spine_terminal.
issues.implementation_latitude: What genuine work the driven spine carries.
hard_constraints_no_gos: Never two crews in one worktree.
local_unknowns: Whether spine_terminal is a check that can fail.

completed_outcomes.outcome: scripts/generate_spine.py ships: a TOML spec with no raw-command field, five typed check kinds each with a generation-time probe, and validate_spine.validate() as the literal last statement before success. Cold-reviewed APPROVE.
completed_outcomes.evidence: Control pairing re-run by the Commander with its own spec: the guarded CLI refused with [falsifiable-unresolved-placeholder] at exit 4 and test ! -f confirmed nothing written; the corrected spec was written. Suite 2765 passed; sweep unchanged at 23.

completed_outcomes.outcome: specs/implementer.spine.toml (gated) and specs/reviewer.spine.toml (survey) generate spines the oracle accepts with zero undecidable. Cold review BLOCKED round 1 and APPROVED round 2.
completed_outcomes.evidence: Both generated spines OK with no undecidable line; the shipped <exact test command> placeholder replaced by selector TestResolverOwnedTokenRegex with min_collect 2, which collects exactly 2. Suite 2775 passed; sweep 23.

completed_outcomes.outcome: A generated spine reached a terminal state under run_crew.py --spine with no handoff and no result path: both items complete, lease released, registry status completed on spine_terminal.
completed_outcomes.evidence: dispatch-proof/spine.json final state read directly; the driven work (positional-argument probing) verified by the Commander catching a wrong positional path and skipping one carrying a resolver-owned token. Suite 2788 passed after map regeneration.

wave_evidence.claim: The generator cannot emit a spine the lint would reject.
wave_evidence.expected: A defect-shaped spec is refused with nothing written; the same spec corrected is written.
wave_evidence.observed: Reproduced by the Commander with an independently authored spec, and again by the cold reviewer with a third: refusal at exit 4 carrying the oracle's own fault text verbatim, output file absent; corrected spec written.

wave_evidence.claim: Every generated gate carries a place to record beliefs, concerns and open questions.
wave_evidence.expected: The handback contract renders on every gate through the engine's own render_human, and each named verb lands where it says.
wave_evidence.observed: 9 of 9 gates across a gated and a survey spine carry it; the reviewer drove attach, flag-candidate and block against a generated spine and each record landed where the contract said.
wave_evidence.source: g1-review-result.md criterion 7 and Commander verification of both generated spines

wave_evidence.claim: A large claim is carried up rather than buried.
wave_evidence.expected: The escalation makes the gate unclosable until an independent reviewer approves.
wave_evidence.observed: TRUE ON GATED ONLY. advance() refuses until an APPROVE review-result is attached. On a survey the engine never consults an artifact postcondition at all -- record() evaluates only command-kind postconditions and consolidate() reads only each item's result field -- so the survey consolidated APPROVE with the escalation unsatisfied and nothing attached.
wave_evidence.source: g2-review-result.md round 1 criterion 7, reproduced against bare checklist_engine dicts

wave_evidence.claim: The spec no longer asks its author to type a shell command from memory.
wave_evidence.expected: No shell text anywhere in either role spec.
wave_evidence.observed: True for shell tokenization and for zero-collect and wrong-population. NOT true for the wrong-invocation class: a positional path is now probed, but a REQUIRED flag the author failed to name is still invisible -- the Commander authored exactly that defect in this run's own dispatch-proof spec and the generator emitted it.
wave_evidence.source: g2-implement-result.md settling-question report, and the blocked gate in dispatch-proof/spine.json

wave_evidence.claim: The shipped corpus is unchanged by this wave.
wave_evidence.expected: validate_spine.py --sweep reports the same 23 fault lines before and after.
wave_evidence.observed: 23 before, 23 after, at every gate boundary; git diff over skills/*/templates/* empty.
wave_evidence.source: g1-integrate.c3 and g2-integrate.c3 engine-run postconditions, plus reviewer re-runs

discrepancies.signal: A Commander cannot drive its own execute.json through the MCP door: mcp_spine_server.py binds one file at import time and offers no per-call spine addressing, while the Commander spine's execute step requires driving a second checklist.
discrepancies.affects: The human's ruling that anything reachable only via the CLI is a defect
discrepancies.evidence: scripts/mcp_spine_server.py:106 SPINE = Path(os.environ['SPINE_FILE']).resolve(); execute.json was driven through checklist_engine.py directly, journaled.
discrepancies.reason: Fixing it is an mcp_spine_server.py change, outside a Commander's latitude. Recorded as tc1 for the Admiral.

discrepancies.signal: record()/consolidate() never evaluate artifact-kind postconditions on a survey item, so no artifact-based gate can be enforced on any survey in the corpus.
discrepancies.affects: Any future plan that assumes an artifact postcondition gates a reviewer or interrogator checklist
discrepancies.evidence: g2-review round 1 drove a generated survey to consolidation APPROVE with the escalation unsatisfied and nothing attached; reproduced against bare checklist_engine dicts.
discrepancies.reason: It changes what a survey-type role spec can promise, so a later wave that migrates reviewer or interrogator templates must plan around it or the engine must change first.

discrepancies.signal: The script probe cannot see a REQUIRED flag the author failed to name -- it verifies only that flags the author DID name exist.
discrepancies.affects: The settling question's answer, which is a headline deliverable
discrepancies.evidence: The Commander authored dispatch-proof m1.c2 omitting --out; the generator emitted it and the oracle accepted it; the driven crew blocked on 'the following arguments are required: --out' at exit 2.
discrepancies.reason: It does not block shipping the generator, but it does block claiming the wrong-invocation class is closed. Resolved by reporting the residual honestly rather than by softening the claim.

discrepancies.signal: recover_crews.py misclassifies a completed spine-only dispatch as NEEDS-ABANDON because its classifier keys on a result artifact such a crew deliberately never writes.
discrepancies.affects: Crew recovery for any future spine-only dispatch
discrepancies.evidence: run_crew.py wrote status=completed with completed_at set and result=None; recover_crews.py then reported NEEDS-ABANDON for the same entry.
discrepancies.reason: It would make a resumed Commander redispatch finished work, which is what recover_crews exists to prevent, but nothing in this wave depends on it. Recorded as tc2.

discrepancies.signal: Adding a module silently staled map/INDEX.md twice this run, surfacing each time as a test failure a crew reasonably misread as pre-existing.
discrepancies.affects: Any wave that adds a module
discrepancies.evidence: 57 modules vs 56 committed after g1; again after the driven change. Both fixed by python -m scripts.code_map build.
discrepancies.reason: Mechanical and already handled; recorded because a crew stashing its own changes cannot distinguish 'not my diff' from 'not this run'.

discrepancies.signal: checklist_engine.load_config json.loads any config_ref that EXISTS, so a config_ref pointing at a real non-JSON file crashes the engine with an unhandled JSONDecodeError before any rail text prints; validate_spine.py has no fault for it.
discrepancies.affects: Any spine or template authored with a mistyped config_ref
discrepancies.evidence: Hit live while wiring this run's own execute.json, which pointed config_ref at a markdown file.
discrepancies.reason: The generator refuses it as spec-config-ref-not-json without moving the oracle; the oracle's own gap is reported rather than patched.
